newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed down on Tuesday with the end of the listings for 1996 reducing fund demand, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active three-day contract plunged to 11.94 percent from 26.80 percent on Monday.
Total turnover decreased to 9.72 million lots from 12 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"The end of domestic share listings this year has led many institutions to reduce their borrowing on the market today, depressing the rates," said one trader.
But traders said they believed the rates would recover early 1997 with the domestic A share markets expected to rise steadily in the year.

Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on institutional buying with the market widely expecting the central bank to cut bank interest rates in the first half of next year, helping to boost state debt prices, traders said.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 rose slightly to 117.60 yuan from 117.58 yuan.
Combined volume of the nine-contract market expanded to 1.53 million lots from 1.22 million.
